comment: Seccomp profile for the assistant-codex service. This container runs the official Codex CLI, whose Node launcher and native runtime need a large, moving syscall set (TTY ioctls, clone3, io_uring probes, memfd, epoll/eventfd variants). A hand-maintained ERRNO allowlist would crash-loop when the runtime reached for an omitted syscall, so this profile is allow-by-default with a denylist of escape-relevant syscalls. It is defense-in-depth on top of cap_drop ALL, no-new-privileges, a read-only root, non-root uid 1000, bounded processes/resources, and isolated networks. Denied syscalls return ENOSYS (38) so runtime fallback paths engage cleanly.

syscalls.comment: Mounting, namespace pivoting and the new fs* mount API are refused by name so nothing can re-enable them by accident.
Kernel module and kexec surface is never needed by the CLI and would provide a direct escape path.
Process tracing and cross-process memory access are unrelated to a chat CLI and could expose neighbouring processes.
eBPF, perf and kernel keyring operations expose broad kernel attack surface unrelated to chat.
Host-wide time, accounting, swap and legacy privileged syscalls are not needed by an unprivileged application container.
